newsitem.title: MALI: Mali's top court scraps election results.
newsitem.headline: Mali's top court scraps election results.

text.p: Mali's constitutional court has scrapped results of the West African country's parliamentary elections, saying numerous irregularities had flawed the chaotic April 13 vote.
The ruling, announced in a special session late on Friday, means that Sunday's planned second round will not take place.
"The court has noted that numerous irregularities seriously tainted the sincerity and transparency of the vote," court president Abdoulaye Dicko said, reading the ruling.
The opposition has demanded the scrapping of the poll, during which organisational problems frustrated many who turned out to vote.
President Alpha Oumar Konare, a historian elected during Mali's widely praised 1992 transition to democracy, had said he would abide by the court's decision.
The election for a 147-seat parliament, to be followed by presidential and municipal elections on May 4 and June 1, was a test of how deeply democracy had taken root in the poor country.
The elections are the second multi-party national polls since independence from France in 1960.
The opposition has been calling for the whole process to be suspended and reorganised and has threatened to disrupt polling if it goes ahead.
Konare, who has steered Mali on a course of economic liberalisation, has said the electoral timetable should be respected. The court did not rule on that issue.
